That swiche a lewed mannes witte shal · pace
The wisdom of an hepe of lerned men
Of maystres hadde he no þen þries ten
Of whiche þer was a · doseyn in þat hous
Worthi to ben Stywardes of Rente and londe
Of my lord þat is in Ingelond
To make hym lyue by his
In honour detteles but þat he were woode
Or lyue als scarsly as hym list desire
And able for to helpen al · a · Shire
In any cas þat myȝt falle or happe
And yet þis manciple sette here alle cappe
¶ The Reue was a sclender colerik man
His berd was Shaue as nygh as euer he can
Hys here was by his eres ful rounde y shorne
His toppe was dokked like a preest by forne
Ful long were his legges and ful lene
Y like a · staf þer was no calf y sene
Wel couthe kepe · a · garner or a bynne
Wel wiste he by the droghte
His lordes shepe his nete his dayerie
His swyn his hors his stoor
Was hoolly in þis Reues gouernyng
And bi his couenant ȝaf þe rekenyng
Syn þat his lord was twenty ȝere of age
Þer couthe no man bringe hym in arrerage
Þer nas baillif ne herd nor other hyne
Þat he knew his sleght and his covyne
Thei were a · drad of hym as of þᵉ dethe
His wonnyng was ful faire vppon an hethe
With grene trees shadewed was his place
He couth better þan his lord purchace
Ful riche was he a stored p
His lord he couthe wel plesen Subtily
To ȝeue and lene hym of his owne gode
And haue a þanke and ȝet a cote
In ȝouthe he hadde lerned a gode mestere
He was a · wel god wriȝt a · Carpentere
This Reue satte vp on a ful good stot
Þat was al pomely gray and highte scot
A · long surcote of peers vppon he hade
And by his side he bare a rusti blade
Of Northfolk was þis Reue of whiche I telle
By side a · toun men clepen it baldeswelle
Tukked he was as is a frere a bowte
And · euer he roode þe hyndrest of on Route
Þat hadde a · fyri cherubynnes face
For sausefleme he was with eyghen narwe
Als hoote he was and lecherous as a sparwe
Of his visage children weren a ferde
Ther nas quyke siluer litarge or bremston
Boras orsure ne oyle of tartre noon
Þat hym myghte helpe of his whelkes white
For of þe knobbes sittyng in his chekes
And for to drink strong wyn rede as blode
Than wold he spek and crie as he were wode
And whan þat he wel dronken hade the wyn
Þan wold he speke no word but latyn
mes hade he two or thre
Þat he hade lerned out of som de cre
No wonder is he herd it al the day
And eke ȝe knowen wel how þat a · Iay
Kan clepe watte as wel as con the pope
But ho so couthe in other þing him grope
Þan hade he spent al his philosophie
He was a gentel harlot and a · kynd
A · better felowe Shul men not fynde
He wold suffre for a quart of wyne
A good felow to haue his concubyne
A twelf monethes and excuse hym atte Fulle
uyli eke a fynche couthe he pulle
And if he fonde owher a gode felowe
He wold techen hym to haue noon Awe
In swiche caas of the Erchedeknes curs
But if mannes soule were in his purse
For in his purs he shuld punysshed be
Purs is þe Erchedeknes helle seide he
But wel I wotte he lyhed riȝt in dede
Of cursyng owȝt eche gilty man hym drede
For curs wille sle riȝt as a · soilyng Sauithe
And also war hym of a significauith
In · daunger hadde he at his owne gise
The ȝonge girles of þᵉ diocise
A · garlond hade he sette vppon his heuede
As grete as it were for an Ale stake
A bokkler hade he made hym of a cake
With hym þer rode a gentel
Ful lowde songe he come hider loue to me
bar to hym a stif burdo
trompe of half so grete a · Sown
doner hade her as ȝelow as wax
But smothe it heng as doth a strike of flax
By ounces heng his lokkes that he hadde
And ther with he his shuldernes ouersprade
But thynne it lay by culpons on
But hode for Iolite wered he noon
For it was trusset vp in his walet
Hym þoughte he roode al of þe newe gette
Discheuele saf his cappe he rode al bare
Swiche glarynge eighen hadde he as an hare
A · vernycle hadde he sewed vppon his cappe
His walet by forn hym in his lappe
A · vois he hade as smale as · a · goote
No berd ne hade he ne neu
As smothe it was as it ware late shaue
I trowe he were a · geldyng or a mare
But of his craft fro Berwik in to ware
Ne was þer swiche an other
For in his male he hade a pylewbere
Whiche þat he saide was oure lady veile
He saide ho hadde a · gobet of the seile
He hadde a · crois of lato
And in a glas he hadde pigges bones
But with these relikes whan þ
Vppon a day he gate hym more money
son and the peple his Apes
But trewli to tellen at the last
He was in chirche A noble
Wel couthe rede a lesson or a story
But alderbest he song an Offertory
For wel he wist whan þat song was song
He moste preche and wil a file his tong
To wynne siluir as he wel coude
Þer fore he song so merily
Now haue I told ȝow sothely in a clause
The state the Array þe nombre
Whi þat assembled was þis cumpanye
In Suthwerk at þis gentel hosterye
That hight þᵉ Tabbard fast by the belle
But now is tyme to ȝow for to telle
How þat we beren vs þat ilke nyght
Whan we were in þat Osterye a light
wil I telle of oure viage
And alle þᵉ remnant of oure pylgrymage
But fyrst I pray ȝow of ȝore curtesie
That ȝe ne ret it nought my vylenye
Thow þat I plenly speke in þis mater
Ne thoughe I speke her wordes
For þis ȝe knowen as welle as I
Who so shal tellen a tale aft
He moote reherce as neyghe as eu
iche a · werd if it be in his charge
Or elles he moote telle his tale vntrewe
Or feyne þinges of fynde wordes newe
He may not spare al þoughe he were his brother
He mote also welle seiȝe o word as an other
Crist spake hym · self ful brode in holy writte
And welle ȝe wote no vileynye is it
Also I pray ȝow for ȝeue it me
Alle haue I not sette foelke in her degre
Here in þis tale as þ
My wytte is short ȝe may wel vnderstonde
Greete chere made oure ost vs eu
And to þe Soper sette he vs a noon
He serued vs with vitailles atte þᵉ beste
Strong was þᵉ wyn and welle drink vs leste
A · semely man oure ooste was withe alle
For to ben an Marchall in an halle
A · large man he was with eyen stepe
A · fairer burges is noon in chepe
Bold of his speche and wis
And of manhode hym lakkid riȝt nouȝt
Eke þerto he was riȝt a mery man
And after soper pleien he by gan
And spake of myrþe a mong oþer þinges
Whan þat we hade made oure rekenynges
And seide þus now lordynges trewli
Ȝe be to me welcom riȝt hertely
For by my trouthen if þat I shal not lye
I seie nought þis ȝere so mery a cumpanye
At oones in þis herberewe as is nowe
Fayn wole I doon ȝow myrth wist I how
And of a myrthe I am right now by þought
Ȝee goon to Canturbury godde ȝo spede
Þe blesseful martir quyte ȝow ȝore mede
And welle I woote as ȝe goon by the way
Ȝe shapen ȝow to tale and to playe
For treweli conford ne myrth nys noon
To ridene by the waie domb as a ston
And therfore wil I maken ȝow disport
As I seid erst and do ȝow som comford
And if ȝow liketh alle by oon assent
For to stonden at my Iugement
And for to wirken as I shal yow seie
To morowen whan we riden by the weie
Now by fader soule þat is dede
But ȝe be merye I wille ȝeue ȝow my hede
Hold vp ȝour hondes with out more speche
¶ Oure conseil was long for to seche
Vs þought it was not worth to make it wise
And bade hym seie his veordit as hym liste
he now herkeneþ for the beste
But take it nought I ȝow preie in disdeigne
Þis is þᵉ poynt to speke short
That eche of ȝow to short w
To Canturbury ward I mene it so
bury ward I mene it so
And homward he shal tellen oþ
Of a ventures whilom þat haue by falle
And whiche of ȝow berithe hym best of alle
Þat is to seien þat telleþ in þis caas
Tales of best sentence and moost solas
Shal haue a · Soper at oure alder coste
Here in this place sittyng bi the poste
Whan þat we comen a gayn fro Cant
And for to make ȝow the more merie
I wille my self godly w
And who so wille my Iugement w
Shal paie alle þat we spende by the weie
And if ȝe vouchesafe þat it be so
And I wille erly shape me therfore
Þat he wold vouche sauf for to do so
And þat he wold be oure gouernoure
And of oure tales Iuge and reportour
And sette a · Soper at a c
And we weln rewled ben at his deuys
In hyegh and low þus by oon assent
We ben a corded to the Iuggement
And þer vppon þe wyn was fet a noon
We dronken and to rest wenten echon
A morwe whan þᵉ day con spring
And gadered vs to gedre in a · floke
And forth we riden a litul more þan pase
Vn to the wateryng of Seynt Thomas
And ther oure oost gan his hors to a reste
And seide lordynges herkenyth if ȝow liste
If euynsong and morwe song a corde
Lat se now ho shal telle þe firste tale
more I drink wyn or ale
Who so be rebelle to my Iuggement
Shal paie for alle þat by the wei is spent
Whiche þat hath þᵉ shorteste shal by gynne
Now draweth cut for þat is myn acord
And ȝe Sir Clerk lat be ȝoure Shamfastnes
Ne studieth nought lay hond to eu
And Shortli for to tellen as it was
Were it by auenture or Sort or cas
Þᵉ Sothe is þis þᵉ Cut fel to the knyght
And tellen he moste his tale as it was reson
As ȝe haue herd what nedith wordes moo
And whan þis godman Saugh þat is was so
As he þat wys was and obedient
To kepen his forward bi his fre assent
He seide sithen · I shal by gynne þe game
What welcome be the Cut a goddes name
Now let vs Ride and herketh what I seie
And with þat word we riden forth oure weie
His tale a noon and seide as ȝe maye here

hilom was as old stories tellen vs
Ther was a · duk þat hight theseus
Of Athenes he was lord and gou
And in his tyme swiche a Conquerour
Þat gretter was noon vnder the sonne
Ful monye a riche contre hade he wone
What with his wisdom and his Chiualrye
And whilom was I clepid scithia
